subject: Subprocessor retention exception & backup purge runbook
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@medihold.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medihold.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention carveout request for audit logs and backup purges

Hi Connor,

Quick context: MediHold is onboarding Redwood for inference on PHI-adjacent workloads. Our security team is reviewing the DPA and the subprocessor matrix. Two items came up in the compliance review that we need help resolving before procurement can sign:

1) Backup purge cadence — Redwood's standard backup purge is listed as 90 days in the onboarding checklist; our audit policy requires 180 days for system and access logs associated with clinical workflows.
2) Subprocessor deletion workflows — we need a documented runbook showing the step-by-step for a retention exception (who authorizes temporary holds, how backups are isolated, and how we get evidence of deletion after the hold is released).

I've attached the excerpt from our DPA and the audit retention requirements workbook for your team to assess. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide a conditional 180-day hold for the specified log buckets?
- Produce attested evidence that a temporary hold was applied and later removed (for our auditors)?

If this is something that needs a DPA addendum or an escrow-style short-term hold, please advise next steps and a rough timeline. We are trying to avoid procurement delays.

Thanks,
Elena Martin
Director, Security & Compliance
MediHold Health

Attachments: medihold-dpa-excerpt.pdf (pdf), audit-retention-reqs.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@medihold.com>
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medihold.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention carveout request for audit logs and backup purges

Elena —

Thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Looping in Kimberly (legal/DPA) and Markus (ops/backup & retention) to scope what we can commit to and the operational runbook. Quick answers up front:

- We can support a temporary retention hold for specific log buckets beyond our default 90-day purge, but it will be implemented as a targeted exception with documented scope and a finite window (we typically do 30/60/180-day increments for exceptions).
- We can provide attested evidence (signed by Ops + Audit logs) showing when the hold was applied and when it was released, and an export of the deletion job run for those objects.

Questions for your team to help us scope the runbook:
- Which specific log types do you need to cover (system auth logs, request traceback, db access logs, etc.)?
- Do you require retention in-place in Redwood's storage, or an escrow snapshot (third-party escrow/air-gapped export)?
- Is 180 days a hard requirement for all environments, or only production clinical tenants?

Proposed next steps/timeline (tentative):
1) Today: Kimberley/Markus review DPA excerpt and draft technical runbook template.
2) +2 business days: Draft retention exception addendum and O&M runbook to share with your security team.
3) +5 business days: Agree on attestation format and sign DocuSign addendum.
4) +10 business days: Implement a one-off canary hold and provide evidence for your audit team.

Markus — can you confirm the operational controls and what evidence artifacts we produce? Kimberly — can you flag any legal or contract-level constraints?

Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: internal: retention-exception-template.md (stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@medihold.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medihold.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention carveout request for audit logs and backup purges

Hi Elena — thanks for raising this. A few contract and evidence notes from Legal: 

1) DPA addendum: We can implement a limited retention exception via a DPA annex (short-term retention addendum). That addendum will:
   - Specify the exact log buckets and tenant IDs in scope.
   - Define the maximum exception window (we can support 180 days but the addendum will require explicit renewal or automatic expiration).
   - Require MediHold to sign a limited-risk acknowledgment covering extra storage and operational overhead.

2) Evidence & attestation: For each exception we will provide:
   - A signed attestation PDF (signed by Redwood Head of Ops and Chief Legal Counsel) describing the scope and dates.
   - An operation trace (s3-like object manifest) showing objects excluded from purge while the hold was active.
   - Post-release deletion report with run timestamps and checksums where applicable.

3) Subprocessor notifications: Because backups can transit our subprocessor storage (cloud buckets / managed backup providers), we will produce an updated subprocessor notice listing which vendors will be involved for the exception window. If needed, we can propose an escrow snapshot option (we would coordinate a one-time export to a mutually agreed storage location and provide chain-of-custody details).

I'll prepare a short DPA annex draft and the runbook template. Connor, Markus — please add any operational constraints below.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dpa-annex-template.docx (docx)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@medihold.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medihold.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention carveout request for audit logs and backup purges

Elena —

Operational details and what we'll deliver for the 180-day exception (assuming MediHold signs the annex):

- Scope: We will tag the specific log buckets and tenant IDs you list. Tags are immutable at exception start and used to exclude objects from the automated purge job.
- Implementation path:
  1) Create retention-exception ticket in our Ops queue with unique exception-id (EXC-DH-4721-01).
  2) Apply object-level retention tags and snapshot a manifest (time-stamped).
  3) Configure purge job to skip tagged objects for the exception window.
  4) Provide daily export of manifest to a secure, read-only bucket for MediHold auditors (access via pre-signed URL).
  5) At exception end: run deletion job, produce deletion manifest (with object ids, timestamps, checksums), and sign attestation.

Evidence artifacts we can produce:
- Exception ticket (EXC-DH-4721-01) with audit trail of approvals.
- Pre-exception snapshot manifest (CSV).
- Daily manifest exports while exception active (CSV).
- Post-deletion report with job run details and checksums (CSV + signed PDF attestation).

Can we do a small canary: 30-day exception on a narrow set of auth logs to validate the process (we'll keep retention metadata and manifests for the auditor)? If MediHold agrees, we can schedule the canary next week after the annex is countersigned.

-Markus
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

--
Redwood internal note: EXC-DH-4721-01 will require 2x Ops approvals and a Legal signoff prior to execution.
